incidents.event_plain: A dozer was moving backwards in an unsafe working condition. Its right track crossed a raised earth edge, so it overturned and caught fire.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for a ground inspection after blasting, proper dozer maintenance, automatic or semi-automatic fire protection, and supervision by an assistant manager and an experienced overman.
incidents.proposed_action: Link machine-release checks, ground inspection and functional fire protection. Treat rollover prevention as a fire-control barrier.
incidents.source_event: While a dozer, not in safe working order was being marched, in reverse direction, the right side track chain of dozer run over berm resulted in topling of dozer. Dozer caught fire causing burn injuries to the operator which proved fatal almost instantly.

incidents.event_plain: A dozer crossed a blasted area above an old underground tunnel containing water and fire. The layer of ground above the tunnel collapsed and the dozer fell into it.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The thickness of ground above the old tunnel had not been established before allowing the dozer to cross. The inquiry called for the precautions in the mining permission and closer management checks on compliance.
incidents.proposed_action: Map old workings and fiery ground. Authorise machine access only after a site-specific ground and thermal assessment.
incidents.source_event: While a dozer was passing through blasted area over an old developed waterlogged fiery galley in an opencast coal mine, due to sudden collapse of parting, the dozer submerged into waterlogged & fiery gallery, resulting into instantaneous death of the dozer operator because of blunt and burn injuries.

incidents.event_plain: Three people were removing an air lock from a Volvo tipper fuel line. They put a 12 V battery-powered wiper pump inside the diesel tank. Bare electrical connections sparked, ignited the fuel-air mixture and sent fire out of the tank opening.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The pump was not designed to work inside a fuel tank. The inquiry called for suitable tools, competent repair workers, written safe repair steps and monitoring of contractor work.
incidents.proposed_action: Use approved repair equipment and an authorised fuel-system maintenance procedure. Verify competence and contractor controls.
incidents.source_event: While crew of 3 persons was trying to remove air-lock from fuel-line of a volvo tipper, a non-submersible 12v DC battery connected wiper motor-pump was put inside its diesel tank whose un-insulated connections resulted in a spark to ignite the fuel-air mixture in the fuel tank. The fire which billowed out from fuel-tank cap resulted serious burn injuries to one helper and minor burn injuries to two other persons. The helper succumbed to his injuries after 10 days while undergoing treatment at hospital.

incidents.event_plain: A water tanker was going to the top of a coal dump to put out a fire at its base. Low diesel supply stopped the engine from receiving fuel and caused steering trouble. The tanker overturned and fell about 11 m, throwing the driver from his seat.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry identified low fuel and failure to use the seat belt. It called for checks of the dump edge and sides before work, and said the tanker should not have been sent to pour water from the top of the dump.
incidents.proposed_action: Plan firefighting access and machine positioning around the ground hazard. Check tanker readiness before deployment.
incidents.source_event: While a water tanker was enroute to top of a coal dump in an open cast coal mine to sprinkle water to quench fire at its toe, tanker engine got deprived of supply of fuel due to less fuel in the tank resulting in malfunctioning of steering thus driver could not control the tanker and it toppled down from a height of 11m throwing driver off the seat, received serious bodily injuries to which he succumbed on the way to hospital.

incidents.event_plain: At night, a contractor worker used a water jet on a burning coal bank while standing about 6 m from its base. Hot material fell from about 10 m and produced a cloud of hot ash and steam. Two dumper operators were nearby, downwind.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The worker was putting out the fire too close to the base of the bank without proper supervision. The inquiry said the written safe working method for firefighting should have been followed.
incidents.proposed_action: Treat suppression as a hazardous job with controlled access, an assessed operating position and a competent supervisor.
incidents.source_event: While a contractor worker was quenching fire in coal bench by water jet standing at a distance of about 6m from the toe of bench in night shift of an open cast coal mine, suddenly hot material of the bench slide from a height of about 10 m forming a cloud of hot ash and steam, causing severe burn injuries to which he succumbed after 8 days in hospital. Two dumper operators standing nearby in wind direction escaped with reportable burn injuries.

incidents.task: Tipper travel at a road junction
incidents.event_plain: An empty 18.8 m3 tipper hit the side of a loaded tipper at a haul-road junction. The collision punctured the loaded tipper fuel tank. Spilled diesel caught fire in both vehicles, and the empty tipper driver was trapped in the damaged cabin.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry said the empty tipper driver did not pay attention to the horn and headlight signals given by the approaching loaded tipper driver.
incidents.proposed_action: Audit junction visibility and traffic controls. Include fuel-release and escape consequences in collision assessments.
incidents.source_event: While an 18.8 m3 empty tipper was on way to loading face it crashed into right side dump body of OB loaded tipper coming from the opposite direction at haul road junction thus punctured the fuel tank of loaded tipper resulting in diesel spill out to catch fire in both the tippers and empty tipper driver unable to escape as was being entrapped in damaged cabin was burned to death.

incidents.original_label: Outbreak of Fire or Spontaneous Heating
incidents.event_plain: Seven people were working on an oil well. A cloud of hydrocarbon gas formed around the work area and a sudden fire spread through it. The inquiry attributes ignition to mobile-phone use.
incidents.inquiry_plain: Gas separation and safe handling were inadequate. The inquiry called for a separator and safe gas disposal through a flare, stopping well activation when the installation manager left and direct supervision was absent, control of phone use, and basic training on workover hazards.
incidents.proposed_action: Verify the gas-handling arrangement before activation. Treat loss of competent supervision as a stop-work condition. Control ignition sources.
incidents.source_event: While a group of seven persons was engaged in workover operations without any statutory supervision in an area which was surcharged with hydrocarbon gas cloud created at the site due to workover operations, when there was a sudden fire because of ignition caused by a mobile telephone operation by one of them, which engulfed the area inflicting severe burn injuries to 06(Six) of them to which one succumbed instantly While remaining 5(five) persons succumed over a period of time in the course of treatment in hospital in the next 20 days.

incidents.event_plain: An excavator was parked at the top of a waste-rock bank during a break. A short circuit started a fire in the cabin while the operator was sleeping inside.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry identified added battery wiring with joints and poor maintenance. It called for automatic fire detection and suppression, checks of the machine and protective devices at the start of the shift, and removal of materials that could burn from the cabin.
incidents.proposed_action: Control wiring modifications, test fire protection and check cabin combustibles. Address exposure during parked-machine breaks.
incidents.source_event: While an excavator was parked at top of overburden bench of an opencast coal mine during break period, the operator's cabin caught fire due to short circuit inflicting serious burn injuries to the operator sleeping inside the cabin, who succumbed to injuries during treatment at hospital after five days.

incidents.task: Preparing to cap a well blowout
incidents.event_plain: Four people were near an oil well that was flowing out of control while preparations were being made to seal it. The well caught fire. Two workers drowned in a nearby water body while escaping.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for a clear emergency plan covering escape routes, prohibited areas, safe meeting points and each person's responsibilities. Everyone at the site should have been told the plan.
incidents.proposed_action: Test actual escape routes around water bodies and pumps. Brief each shift on exits, restricted areas, assembly and accountability.
incidents.source_event: While four persons were working in the vicinity of well plinth area to drench the blowout for preparation to cap the well, suddenly the blowout caught fire and in the process of escaping from that area two persons were drowned in the water body existing near the pumps and died.

incidents.event_plain: About 54 m3 of hot waste rock slid from a dump about 30 m high and trapped two contractor workers below it.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for cooling of the hot material, fencing of the unsafe area and worker training. The event account does not clearly state that there was a fire.
incidents.proposed_action: Retain as a thermal-hazard sensitivity case. It supports exposure separation but is excluded from the main fire count.
incidents.source_event: While two contractual persons were present in unsafe area below dumped hot overburden of height about 30m, of an opencast coal mine, suddenly about 54 Cu. m of hot overburden slide from top in which both were entrapped and received burn injuries, causing death of one person after about 25 Hrs. 30 minutes during treatment and the other survived with disability.

incidents.event_plain: A senior overman was supervising filling and dozing on cracked, unstable ground. He walked towards smoke about 50 m away. The ground gave way beneath him and he fell into a hot hole.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for ground-stability checks, risk assessment, safe filling methods, maps of old underground workings, emergency plans, training and drills. Smoke and hot ground are recorded, but the event does not clearly establish a fire.
incidents.proposed_action: Retain as a thermal-hazard sensitivity case. Avoid foot inspection of unstable hot ground without an assessed access method.
incidents.source_event: While a Senior Overman was engaged for supervision of fly ash filling and dozing operation at the unstable and cracks formed ground, in the meantime he saw smoke coming out at a distance of 50m from fly ash filling area, subsequently he went there on foot to inspect the smoke coming out from newly formed crack, suddenly a pothole was occurred just beneath his feet where he was standing and inspecting the place resulting he fell inside the hot pot hole and body was not recovered till date.

incidents.task: Excavator at a burning dump toe
incidents.event_plain: An excavator was cleaning and levelling a haul road at the base of a burning waste dump. The bank was 11 m high with a 55-degree slope. Hot material rolled down, broke the upper part of the front glass and entered the cabin.
incidents.inquiry_plain: Work continued below a known fire. The inquiry cited a bank height of no more than 3 m and a slope of no more than 37.5 degrees for this case. It also called for prompt fire control, inspection before machine deployment, contractor coordination and safety briefing of workers.
incidents.proposed_action: Keep people and machines outside the hot-material runout zone. Require a ground and thermal review before restarting work.
incidents.source_event: While a excavator was deployed for cleaning and levelling haul road near toe of the bench made in the in-pit waster dump of height 11m & slope 55 degree having fire in an opencast coal mine, a chunk of heated material roll down from the bench and fragmented heated limp pieces pierced in to the operator cabin by breaking over portion of the front glass, causing burn injury to the operator who succumbed while undergoing treatment at a hospital after three and half days of the accident.

incidents.event_plain: A lamp fitter was lighting a flame safety lamp. A burning match fell on a cleaning cloth partly soaked in fuel. The cloth caught fire and then set her clothing on fire.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for care while lighting lamps and suitable protective clothing. Lamp lighting should have been on a separate table from cleaning and refilling. A suitably certified person should have maintained and checked the lamps.
incidents.proposed_action: Separate lighting from fuel handling. Control contaminated wiping materials and provide suitable work clothing.
incidents.source_event: While a female lamp fitter was igniting a flame safety lamp, suddenly the burning match stick dropped on a wiping cloth, partially soaked with fuel, causing fire on it which incidentally initiated fire on her saree (due to fall of fired wiping cloth) sustaining serious burn injury which proved fatal after 12 days in the hospital during treatment.

incidents.task: Excavator below a burning coal rib
incidents.event_plain: An excavator loaded waste rock below an old dump about 11 m high with a 72-degree slope. A remaining coal band, about 2.5-3.5 m thick, was burning. Hot pieces rolled down, broke the front glass and entered the cabin.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The excavator worked too close to the burning bank and the work rules were not enforced. The inquiry cited a bank height of no more than 3 m and a slope of no more than 37.5 degrees for this case. Work below the bank should have stopped until the fire or heating was put out.
incidents.proposed_action: Apply a controlled exclusion zone and a documented restart decision. Cabin glazing does not replace separation from falling hot material.
incidents.source_event: While an excavator was deployed for loading of overburden from an old overburden dump of about 11m in height and sloped at about 72 degrees having fire in remnant rib of coal seam about 2.5-3.5m thickness in an opencast coal mine, a chunk of heated material roll down from the highwall side of the bench and broken hot lumps pierced in to the operator cabin by breaking the front glass, causing burn injury to the operator to which he succumbed on the spot.

incidents.event_plain: Four workers were at a pump station about 14 m from the base of burning ground. During heavy rain, about 154.72 m3 of hot material fell from a height of about 70.40 m, producing steam and hot ash around them.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The pump station was in an unsafe position and the risk to workers had not been properly assessed. Workers were not moved away in time despite the danger from fire and heavy rain.
incidents.proposed_action: Include rainfall and hot-ground changes in withdrawal triggers. Relocate occupied workstations outside the credible runout area.
incidents.source_event: While four workmen were engaged at a pump station at a distance of about 14m from the toe of side of an opencast coal mine, having fiery strata; about 154.72 Cu.m of hot strata dislodged from a height of about 70.40m during heavy rain, emanating cloud of steam and hot ash causing burn injuries to them; to which one of them succumbed in hospital next day, another succumbed in hospital after twelve days and remaining two joined duty after recovery.

incidents.event_plain: A contractor worker was moving a water hose from the top of an old ramp to a lower working level. He slipped from the ramp edge and fell into hot ash at its burning base.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for a co-worker or supervisor to accompany the worker at the remote work site, proper firefighting training, and suitable protective equipment and fire-resistant clothing.
incidents.proposed_action: Plan hose access with a buddy/supervisor and safe footing. Verify task-specific training and protective clothing.
incidents.source_event: While a contractor worker was trying to bring a water hose pipe from top of the old ramp to bottom bench, slipped from the edge of the ramp and fell on hot ash at the bottom edge of ramp on fire, inflicted burn injury which resulted into fatality during the treatment at the hospital.

incidents.event_plain: A worker climbed a steep shortcut between working levels using a flexible pipe for support. He fell about 10 m among loose rocks.
incidents.inquiry_plain: The inquiry called for a risk-based safety plan that included firefighting on hot ground, proper supervision and marked walking routes. Firefighting is mentioned in the inquiry, but the event does not confirm that he was fighting a fire at the time.
incidents.source_event: While a person was taking a short cut route from lower to upper bench, along high & almost vertical sides of excavation, containing loose boulders precariously hanging, in support of 4canvas make flexible pipe range laid along the sides, in an opencast coal mine, he fell down from a height of 10m and received serious bodily injuries due to fall of rolling loose boulders to which he succumbed while being shifted to company's nearby Jealgora Hospital.
